support_reason: Fully implemented and fully auditable. This is THE BENCHMARK every model must beat and the system's explainable fallback when every model is switched off. Per-feature contributions are stored in ORIGINAL UNITS so a reviewer can reconstruct the score by hand from the weights in config/parameters.yaml.

CUSUM and EWMA on monthly normalised provider VALUE and FREQUENCY both run, with cfg.min_history_periods enforced before a change point may be declared, and pre-change mean, post-change mean, change date and confidence stored for every one. MIX and DENIAL behaviour are unavailable (no codes, no remittance) and the signal names which metrics were evaluated.

Isolation Forest and Local Outlier Factor are trained on a strictly earlier period with entity isolation, scored on a later one, explained with SHAP in original units beside the peer value, and monitored for drift. The disposition is MONITOR_ONLY — the catalogue's own choice — and the safety boundary makes it impossible for this control to be anything else. Whether it adds lift beyond R01/R02 is DECIDED BY THE PROMOTION GATE at run time and reported honestly either way.

HDBSCAN over the residual space produces candidate clusters for the quarterly typology review. Disposition is MONITOR_ONLY only, and no production action follows until a human converts a cluster into an authored rule — which itself enters the registry in shadow status and requires a separate approver.

On a file with service lines the proxy (the diagnosis-procedure mismatch flag) is replaced by the catalogue's own measure: each provider's share of graded visits billed at the top level of their code family, shrunk toward specialty peers and cut at the peer percentile. Case mix and setting are not risk-adjusted beyond the specialty peer group.

Implemented as an interpretable EXPECTED-AMOUNT residual rather than an expected-LEVEL residual: the expectation is built from primary diagnosis, length of stay and policy type (age and setting are unavailable), and the residual is robust (median/MAD). This is the same shape of control against a coarser target, and it is classified PARTIAL because 'level' does not exist in the source.

Runs ONLY against clearly-labelled SYNTHETIC discharge summaries generated by this artefact (data/synthetic_documents/, every filename and body marked SYNTHETIC). the claim extract contains no documents. Every finding carries a source span, and a finding without a span is discarded by the pipeline rather than shown with a caveat.

Runs on the billed service lines and the level of each code within its family, tracking each provider's monthly share of top-level services. Case-mix change is approximated by the mix of main-diagnosis chapters, and a contract or ownership change is read from the provider and contract records rather than from a full structural-change register.

Runs when the file carries every diagnosis in order and a grouper table saying which secondary diagnoses raise the payment band. The grouper is a stand-in rather than a certified DRG grouper, and 'supporting evidence' is read from the patient's other claims, the services billed and the medicines dispensed, not from the clinical record.

Runs when the file carries the ordered diagnoses and the grouper's complication flags. Risk adjustment uses the main-diagnosis chapter mix of all providers and excludes transfers; age and specialty adjustment are not applied.

Runs on the patient's diagnoses across all their claims in this file, the grouper's severity flags and any medicines dispensed. History from other insurers is not available, so only this payer's longitudinal record is read.

Runs on the ordered diagnosis list and present-on-admission flags. The coding policy applied is a fixed set of general sequencing rules (one main diagnosis, no repeated codes, no external-cause main diagnosis, main diagnosis present on admission outside obstetric, newborn and transfer cases), not an effective-dated national coding-policy table.

Runs on each provider's monthly average grouper severity of inpatient stays and checks length of stay and services per stay for a matching shift. A shift in referrals is not checked, and service-line expansion is approximated by the main-diagnosis chapter mix.

Runs on icd_code_matches_procedure = False, which is a boolean VERDICT with no procedure behind it: it records that some upstream process judged a mismatch, without the evidence for that judgement. The disposition is therefore DOWNGRADED from the catalogue's first-named REJECT to the pend limb: a denial is permitted only on an objective, effective-dated condition this system can evaluate itself, and another system's undocumented verdict is not one. The same field also feeds CLN-01-R01 as a provider-level rate.
Runs as the catalogue specifies when the file carries service lines, the patient's diagnoses and a curated table of the diagnoses that support each service, with the configured look-back.

Runs on service lines and a care-pathway table of services that must follow another within a window, and allows for work-ups done elsewhere when a referral into the provider is on record. The 'prerequisite result' limb is not checked separately from the prerequisite service.

Runs on service lines and each provider's specialty, measuring how often a provider bills codes that other providers of its specialty almost never bill. Combinations with the ordering or rendering clinician are not used.

On a file with service lines the proxy (same principal diagnosis within a fixed interval) is replaced by the catalogue's own test: the same activity code for the same patient on another claim inside that code's minimum interval in the repeat-interval policy, excluding lines with a repeat indicator, a failed earlier result, and oncology, dialysis or maternity pathways. Equivalent (not identical) codes are not grouped.

On a file with service lines the proxy (any claims in a window) is replaced by service days per patient and service family in a trailing window, compared with the peer percentile for that family, excluding inpatient stays and oncology, dialysis and maternity pathways. Age risk adjustment is not applied.

Runs on service lines, recorded results and the repeat-interval policy's list of tests that need a result before a repeat. The 'unchanged result' limb is not implemented; only an absent (or only later recorded) earlier result is flagged.

Claims per distinct member at a provider is computable and is shrunk toward the peer mean. 'Services' is substituted by 'claims' because there are no service lines, so the intensity of each claim is invisible to this control.

Runs on referrals and the claims they led to, comparing each referring provider's follow-on spend per referral with other referrers. Whether the first visit was low-intensity is shown but not used as a filter, and specialty pathways are not modelled.

Runs as specified. Length of stay and primary diagnosis both exist, so the diagnosis-peer robust residual is exactly the control the catalogue describes. Risk adjustment is by diagnosis rather than DRG, which the catalogue permits ('DRG/diagnosis').

Runs as specified: discharge_readmit_gap_days is present for every claim and is compared against cfg.readmit_window_days, with the episode's payment impact attached. The catalogue's own words — 'Episode review, NOT FRAUD LABEL' — are reproduced on the signal so a reviewer sees them.

Multi-claim episodes at the same provider with a short gap are detectable. The disposition is PENDED rather than REPRICED because the correct combined payable amount is not computable without a payment policy or tariff, and reserves REPRICE for the case where it is.

Runs on encounters: each hospital's unplanned admissions as a share of its emergency and outpatient attendances plus those admissions, against the rate expected from its main-diagnosis mix, with observation stays not counted. Outpatient attendances stand in for emergency presentations, which the file records only sparsely, and severity beyond the diagnosis chapter and referral mix are not adjusted for.

Runs on imaging lines and the reports or results linked to them, after the latency allowance. Laboratory results are left to CLN-08-R03; therapy administration records are not carried by the file, so therapy lines are not checked.

The 'verified operating period' limb cannot run (no operating periods). The 'no credible operating footprint' limb is implemented as a composite of the undated blacklist flag plus a thin, bursty claim footprint, and the signal states which limb fired. SIU_LEAD is the catalogue disposition and is retained — this control never denies.

On a file with service lines the proxy (diagnosis, stay length and amount) is replaced by an identical line-level signature (codes, units, amounts and start times) recurring for several different patients at one provider, excluding inpatient packages, laboratory panels and dispensing. Clinical notes are not compared.
Runs as the catalogue specifies when the file carries member service confirmations and independent attendance records, discarding unverified channels and answers given too long after the service.

Runs on repeatedly billed drug-treated conditions and looks for any dispensed medicine or recorded result for the patient, compared with other patients with the same condition. Follow-up visits are not counted as a footprint and out-of-network care cannot be seen.
Runs as the catalogue specifies when service lines name the rendering clinician and the code reference gives the minimum time per service, excluding laboratory, imaging, dispensing and team services.

Concurrent inpatient occupancy per provider per day is computable from admission and discharge dates and is compared against cfg.provider_daily_capacity_admissions × cfg.capacity_tolerance_multiple. The capacity figure is a CONFIGURED PLACEHOLDER, not a licensed bed count — the catalogue's own note that 'missing roster produces low confidence' applies directly, and the signal's confidence is reduced accordingly.

Runs on service lines and the provider's scarce-equipment inventory (machines, minutes per use, operating hours). Capacity is checked per day rather than by overlapping start and end times within the day.

Monthly claim throughput per provider is computable, and a CUSUM change point on it is exactly the shape of this control. What cannot be done is the EXCLUSION: without staff, hours or facility-change records there is no way to segment a legitimate expansion from a suspicious jump, so every signal carries that caveat and the disposition stays an audit.

Runs on laboratory lines and the clinician roster: a test with no ordering clinician, an unknown one, or one without a valid licence or ordering role is flagged, excluding screening diagnoses and standing orders. The 'qualifying encounter or indication' limb is left to CLN-03-R02.

Runs on laboratory lines and panel definitions: a panel billed together with its own components, or every component billed separately above the panel price, excluding reflex tests. Whether a panel exceeds what was ordered is not checked because orders are not itemised.

Runs as the catalogue specifies when the file carries laboratory lines, their payments and their results: a paid test with no result after the latency allowance, or an identical multi-value result set reported for unrelated patients.

Runs on laboratory lines that name a performing laboratory other than the billing provider, comparing the billed price with what that laboratory charges itself. Contract permissions for reference-laboratory arrangements are not read.

Runs on laboratory lines and the code reference's complexity marker, comparing each provider's shrunk rate of genetic or high-complexity tests with peers and excluding oncology, genetics and haematology centres. Patient-risk adjustment is not applied.

Runs as the catalogue specifies when the file carries claim lines, the policy that says which document each service needs, and the documents attached to each claim: a required document type that is still absent once the governed deadline after submission has passed is flagged, and a claim whose deadline has not yet passed is not.

Runs against the clearly-labelled SYNTHETIC discharge summaries this artefact generates (every filename and body marked SYNTHETIC), never against real documentation, because the claim extract contains none. Extracted diagnosis and stay length are compared field-by-field against the claim, each with its own precision threshold, and every rendered finding carries its exact source span.

Searches the claim's readable clinical documents for each fact the medical-necessity policy requires for the billed service, counting a fact mentioned only in a negated sentence as absent. The search is for the policy's words and phrases, not a clinical reading of the note, and a claim with no readable clinical document is skipped because absence would prove nothing.

Compares the services named in the approval request (activity codes and their reference descriptions, each with its exact text span) with the lines billed under that approval, and flags a billed service of a different family that the request never mentions. Entity-level comparison only: a paraphrase that names no code or reference description is not understood.

Runs against the SYNTHETIC corpus only. Boilerplate is stripped before comparison, as the catalogue requires, and similarity is computed on the patient-specific remainder. Because the corpus is generated from templates, a baseline similarity is expected and the threshold (cfg.doc_clone_similarity_threshold) is set above it — a limitation stated on every signal.

Reads the age, sex and sex-specific findings a note states, each with its exact span and an OCR-adjusted confidence, and compares them with the patient's registration record. The laterality limb does not run because the claim lines carry no body side to contradict.

Compares each later version of a claim's document with the version it replaces when it was written after a denial on that claim (or the claim it resubmits), and flags changed or added payment-relevant facts that are not a signed addendum. 'Payment-relevant' is a fixed list of extracted fields (stay, dates, diagnosis, procedure, severity, indication, units), not every fact a clinician could change.

Measures how much patient-specific narrative each note for a high-complexity service contains once template lines are removed, compares it with notes of the same type and language (within specialty where the peer group is large enough), and flags providers where most such notes are far thinner than peers write. 'Generic' is measured by length of patient-specific wording, not by clinical content.

Runs as the catalogue specifies when the file carries each member's cover periods with real start and end dates and the enrolment event log: every service date is checked against the cover in force, with the grace, newborn, emergency and pending-backdated-change (retroactive update) exceptions applied.

Runs when the file carries claim lines, each member's product, the dated benefit schedule and a code reference that maps each service to its benefit family: each line is checked against the benefit version in force, allowing mandatory benefits, approved exceptions and self-paid lines.

Runs when the file carries benefit limits, claim lines and payments: what was already paid for the benefit in the cover period (reversals and pending approvals left out) is added to the amount now claimed and compared with the limit, per member or per family as the benefit row says.

Runs when the file carries each member's network and each provider's dated network status: the provider is checked against the member's network on the service date, and, where the benefit schedule and referral records are present, a required referral is looked for; emergencies and access gaps are excluded.

Runs when member records carry a protected national-ID reference with date of birth and sex: records sharing one reference but disagreeing on date of birth or sex are raised, leaving out placeholder IDs and newborns and never matching on names.

Runs when member records carry a date of death with its source and reliability: services starting after that date plus the reporting margin are raised, unless the source is unreliable or the claim is only an administrative item.

The OVERLAPPING-ENCOUNTER limb runs: admission and discharge dates exist, so two inpatient stays for one member that overlap in time are detectable. The TRAVEL-SPEED limb does not run — there is no geography. Dates carry no time component, so a same-day transfer cannot be distinguished from a genuine overlap and confidence is reduced accordingly.

Runs the two limbs the file supports: same-day use of one member's cover in different emirates, and services that do not fit the member's age or sex, requiring at least two independent observations. The chronic and rare-disease pathway exclusion is not modelled, so the reviewer must check it.

Runs when the file carries dated facility licences and clinician licence dates: the facility and the treating and ordering clinicians are each checked on the service date, with the approved grace period applied.

provider_blacklist_flag is the only exclusion-list signal available and it is UNDATED, so 'effective match at service time' cannot be evaluated. The catalogue permits REJECT only on an exact, effective-dated identifier match; with no effective date the governed disposition is downgraded to PREPAY_PEND, which is the treatment the catalogue itself prescribes for a non-exact match.

Runs when the clinician roster (or the provider status register) records privileges, including services a clinician or facility is explicitly not permitted to perform: a line for such a service is raised unless an approved authorisation covers it.

Runs when the file names the treating clinician on each line and the roster records their specialty and privileges: each service is compared with the governed specialty map, and cross-specialty privileges are honoured.

Runs the volume-and-value limb: a provider newly credentialed, relicensed or resuming after a long gap whose early billing tops the peer percentile for its facility type, excluding acquisitions. The 'lacks an expected operating footprint' limb needs staffing and site data the file does not hold.

Runs when claim lines carry the treating clinician and a roster lists valid clinicians: services that need a clinician but carry none, the facility's own code, or an ID on no roster are returned for correction.

Runs two explicit role rules: the treating clinician must be on the billing facility's roster unless an in-house clinician ordered the service, and a non-independent role may not bill a physician-level service alone. The file has no supervising-clinician field, so the ordering clinician stands in for the supervisor.
Runs when claim lines carry start and end times: each clinician's overlapping timed services are counted against the governed maximum, leaving out anaesthesia, team procedures and date-only records.

Runs the leave limb as specified (services dated inside a clinician's recorded leave). The travel limb uses emirate-level location and one governed minimum travel time between emirates, a stand-in for facility-to-facility travel times the file does not hold.
Runs when the code reference lists the facility types each service may be billed from and the provider register records each provider's licensed type; home, mobile and telehealth visits are excepted.

Checks that inpatient, intensive-care and day-case billing has an encounter with admission, bed and discharge records, excepting transfers and records too recent to have arrived. The 'required observation trail' limb is not run because no policy in the file says which observations a stay requires.

Compares claims from the same provider for the same patient: an outpatient visit billed inside an inpatient stay (or on the same encounter) is a setting conflict, excluding transfers. The file does not separate professional-fee from facility claims, so claims from one provider stand in for the professional/facility pair.

Runs when every claim has an encounter type: each provider's monthly share of inpatient and day-case claims is split at its best change point and the later share is compared with peers of the same facility type, excluding ownership or contract changes.

Checks each telehealth visit's services against the code reference's remote-eligibility flag and, where the register records telehealth privileges, the provider's privilege on the date. The member-geography limb is not run: the file holds no rule on where a patient may be seen from.

Runs when telehealth encounters carry their duration and the file holds the prescriptions and referrals that follow them: a remote visit that led to an order but lasted less than the policy minimum, or lacks a note where this provider's notes are normally present, is raised.

Runs when the file carries prescriptions (and referrals) with prescriber and pharmacy or recipient: each telehealth provider's top supplier share is compared with the governed threshold and with other prescribing providers, excluding shared ownership and narrow networks.

Runs when the file carries consultations, the prescriptions and referrals that follow them, and a drug policy marking high-cost products: each telehealth provider's rate of visits turning into a high-cost order is compared with other consulting providers.

There are no referral edges in the claim extract. The implemented edge is AGENT→PROVIDER co-occurrence: the share of an agent's claims flowing to their single most-used provider, plus the Herfindahl index of that agent's provider distribution. That is a distribution-channel concentration, not a clinical referral, and the signal says so. The peer comparison is by agent portfolio size, not by specialty or geography, because neither is available.

Runs on the file's DIRECTED provider-to-provider referrals: a pair is flagged when both directions carry a minimum count and each is several times stronger than the recipient's share of all referrals predicts. The multidisciplinary-team exclusion is approximated by the declared owner: two providers under one owner are treated as one organisation's team.

Links each referral to the claim it produced and counts it as converted when that claim carries a top-tail line value; a recipient is flagged when its conversions far exceed the number expected for the same recipient specialty and referral reason, with a Poisson tail test. 'High cost' is a percentile of the file's own line values rather than a payer-defined list of high-cost services.

Follows each referrer's referrals to laboratories, imaging centres and pharmacies and flags a referrer whose downstream referrals stay mostly with providers sharing its bank account, phone or address under a different declared owner. A disclosed common owner, and a narrow network recorded on the payer's contracts, are excluded. The dense-group test is the retained share of referrals, not a full community detection.

Runs as the catalogue specifies when the provider register carries bank, phone, address and owner identifiers: legally distinct providers sharing an exact token are linked, providers under one declared owner are treated as a known group, and a token shared by many providers is treated as a shared service. Exact matches only; device identifiers are not in the file.

Louvain communities are computed on the real member-provider-agent-TPA graph built from the claim extract, with weekly time-bounded snapshots, and internal density is compared against SIZE-matched communities. Peer matching on specialty and geography is not possible, so the comparison is size-only and the signal records that.

The TIME and AMOUNT limbs run: claims within a community that share an admission date and a closely-matching amount are a synchronisation signature. The CODE and RESUBMISSION limbs do not (no codes, no lineage). The catalogue already assigns this control 'supporting evidence' status and MONITOR_ONLY, which is retained.

Tracks each provider's monthly rank by distinct members served and flags a move from the edge to the centre of the network with material value, excluding a new contract, a merger with a same-owner provider and a newly credentialed provider; a recorded ownership change is reported alongside. Centrality is measured by members served, not by a full graph-centrality score.

Member-provider pair frequency and total value are directly computable and are compared against the distribution of all dyads. The BENEFIT-EXHAUSTION limb is unavailable (no benefit limits) and the signal states that only two of the three conditions were evaluated.

Flags a provider whose patients come overwhelmingly from one employer or sponsor, far beyond that employer's share of members in the provider's own emirate, when the group's claims stay with the same few providers. On-site and occupational clinics are excluded. Catchment is judged by emirate; visit location is not used.

Flags a provider where claims with no patient share (on products that normally charge one) and patients with repeated top-tail services are both several times the rate across all providers, and enough patients show both. The non-medical substitution limb is reported only when dispensing records exist, and approved programmes are recognised only through products whose benefit rules charge no share.

Runs as the catalogue specifies when the file carries member confirmations and complaints: evidence counts only when it is tied to the patient's own claim at that provider through an authenticated channel, and a provider is escalated when several distinct patients independently report a service, item or charge they did not receive.

This control requires CONFIRMED REVIEW OUTCOMES as its label, and the catalogue is explicit that raw system flags must never be used as one. review_outcome is empty at load, and fraud_label is held-out evaluation data that no detection component may read. Implementing it against fraud_label would be precisely the leakage this artefact is built to prevent. It becomes executable once the artefact has accumulated real reviewer dispositions.

Agent (originator) → provider concentration is computable and is the structural content of this control. Employer groups do not exist in the source, so only the agent limb runs, and the employer-clinic exclusion cannot be applied — stated on every signal.

Early tenure (cfg.early_tenure_days) and claim value both exist, so clustering of high-value early-tenure claims by AGENT is computable. 'Beyond morbidity expectation' is approximated by the diagnosis-peer amount distribution rather than a morbidity model. The catalogue's instruction — 'review, NEVER INDIVIDUAL DENIAL' — is reproduced on the signal.

Looks for one identifier value that appears on actors of different kinds — a clinic's recorded owner who is also the agent who sold its patients' policies, or an employer or patient identifier — using exact matches only, and excludes on-site employer clinics as known corporate links. The file has no device identifiers and no contact details for agents, so those links cannot be seen.

Runs at CLAIM-HEADER level, not line level: the match key is payer + member + provider + primary diagnosis + admission date + discharge date + exact requested amount. Without activity codes and units this is a strictly coarser key than the catalogue specifies, so it can miss a duplicated line inside a differing claim. Because it is an exact, objective, hard-edit condition it retains the REJECT disposition — but only the later claim in the active lineage is rejected.

Runs on member + provider + primary diagnosis within cfg.duplicate_window_days with amounts within cfg.duplicate_amount_tolerance. There is no code-equivalence map, so 'code equivalent' is approximated by identical primary diagnosis, which is weaker.

Episodes are built from same-member readmission proximity, so a multi-claim episode with a repeated primary diagnosis is detectable. 'Component service' is not — there are no components. Disposition is downgraded to PREPAY_PEND because a correct repriced amount cannot be COMPUTED without line-level detail, and permits REPRICE only where the correct payable amount is computable.

Runs as the catalogue specifies when the file carries this payer's payments, the other insurers' payments matched through a privacy-protected reference, and the coordination-of-benefits records. The file carrying the other insurer's payment is taken as the authorised data sharing; the reviewer is asked to confirm it.

Runs as the catalogue specifies when the file carries claim lines and an effective-dated bundling edit table: a parent and its separately charged component on one claim, with the edit's own modifier rule deciding whether an indicator separates them.

Runs on claim lines and the bundling edit table across different claims for the same patient. Two parts are approximated: the global or episode window is a fixed number of days around the parent procedure (the file carries no per-contract global periods), and the contractual professional/facility split is recognised from professional and technical component indicators rather than from contract terms.

Runs on claim lines and package definitions. Charging for a component the package includes at zero price is checked exactly. The definition does not say which components are mandatory, so the required core of each package is taken as the listed components found on nearly every claim for it, and only packages with enough claims are checked for missing activities. A documented medical omission is recognised only from a claim document typed as an omission note.

Runs on claim lines, line-level payments and the package definitions, which serve as the inclusion list for package and case-rate codes. Components the definition marks as separately payable are the carve-outs. The inclusion list carries no effective dates, and there is no DRG grouper assigning case rates, so only case rates billed as package codes are checked.

Runs on claim lines, providers with their type and specialty, the bundling edit table and the code reference: separately charged code pairs no edit covers, billed together by one provider far more often than by its peers, with rates shrunk toward the peer rate and a minimum volume. Which pairs can be components of one service is approximated as codes of the same service family, since the file has no component relationships beyond the edit table itself.

Runs on claim lines (and diagnoses) against the code-set table of valid codes and their effective dates. The lines do not state which code-set version they were coded under, so each code is checked against its own validity dates on the service date, and 'absent' is judged only for types of service the code set covers.

Runs as the catalogue specifies when the file carries claim lines, each patient's date of birth and sex, and the explicit age and sex restrictions of each activity code. An approval covering the very code is taken as the policy-approved clinical exception.

Runs on claim lines against the maximum units per day, summed per patient per day across claims, and per day of stay on inpatient claims. The policy table holds daily maxima only, so episode maxima are not checked; drug dose limits are left to the pharmacy controls.

Runs as the catalogue specifies when the file carries claim lines with start and end times and the minutes each time-based code represents: billed minutes beyond the recorded window, and one clinician's timed services overlapping (anaesthesia excepted), both after the rounding tolerance.

Runs as the catalogue specifies when the file carries claim lines, the benefit rules that say which service families need approval under each product, and the approvals themselves. Emergencies and services with a pending or deemed request are excluded.

Runs as the catalogue specifies when claim lines carry approval references and the file carries the approvals with their status and validity dates. Another approval covering the date is taken as an extension, and an emergency shortly before the approval started as the urgent retrospective route.

Runs as the catalogue specifies when claim lines carry approval references and the file carries the approved codes, provider and facility: the billed code, provider or facility differs from what was approved, with equivalent codes and recorded transfers accepted.

Runs as the catalogue specifies when claim lines carry approval references and the file carries approved units and values and the payment records: the running total claimed against each approved line, excluding reversed or cancelled lines, compared with what was approved.

Runs on claim lines' approval references against the patient each approval was issued to: an approval consumed by another patient, with family sharing allowed only when policy permits. Reuse by another provider and use after exhaustion are reported by the scope and quantity controls of the same scenario rather than here.

Runs on claim-line indicators against the prohibitions the file carries: indicator prohibitions in the payment-policy table where present, and bundling edits that do not allow a modifier to separate a pair. There is no complete code-by-indicator policy table, so a pair neither source prohibits is not reported.

Runs on claim-line indicators, line Observations and claim documents. Which indicators need a supporting report is a governed parameter list rather than a policy table carried in the file, and any document on the claim is accepted as support.

Runs as the catalogue specifies when the file carries claim-line indicators and providers with their type and specialty: each provider's use rate of each indicator, shrunk toward its peers, above the peer percentile and a multiple of the peer mean, with a minimum denominator.

Runs on claim lines, line-level payment decisions and the bundling edits. The edit-launch timeline is taken from each edit's effective-from date, since the file carries no separate rule-launch log, and a provider education period after launch is ignored.

Runs as the catalogue specifies when the file carries claim lines, the effective-dated tariff by network tier and the provider contracts with their tier and discount: a unit price above the allowed price beyond the rounding tolerance is repriced. Carved-out contracts are excluded; all amounts are in AED and VAT is not itemised in this file.

The full equation (gross − discount − patient_share = net) cannot be checked because patient_share is absent. The one limb that CAN be checked is checked: approved must not exceed requested, and neither may be negative. That is a genuine transaction-integrity edit and it runs at INGEST.

Runs as specified except that the peer comparison is at PRIMARY-DIAGNOSIS level rather than activity-code level, because there are no activity codes. Robust median/MAD residuals are used, not mean/SD z-scores, because claim amounts are heavily right-skewed.
Both limbs run: requested and approved amounts exist for every claim, so a provider's approval-ratio level and its VARIANCE are both computable against shrunk peers.

Recalculates each claim's patient share from the member's product and the benefit terms in force for every billed service, and compares it with the share on the claim. Deductible accumulators are not in the file, so a share above the calculation is raised at reduced confidence rather than excused.
Runs the catalogue equation (billed amount less discount less patient share must equal the amount claimed from the insurer) on every claim that carries all four amounts.

Compares each provider's rate of zero or rounded-down patient shares, on claims whose benefit terms require a share, with the rate expected for the same products across all providers; zero-share benefits and regulator programmes are left out.

Compares what members' receipts show they paid the provider with the approved patient share on the claim, and adds member complaints about overcharging; receipts for non-covered items with documented consent are left out.

Checks every correction, resubmission and cancellation in the claim-version history for a missing, self-referencing or non-existent original, or an original belonging to a different member, provider or payer.

Compares each resubmission of a refused claim with the refused version (diagnosis, codes, units, provider, setting) and pends changes that the governed correction matrix does not accept for the refusal reason.
Follows each resubmission chain back to its original service and counts the attempts, leaving out formal appeals, and the distinct sets of changes made before the service was paid.

Compares each provider's success rate on changed resubmissions after a refusal with other providers, using shrinkage, and requires the successes to concentrate on one refusal reason. Billing-vendor and policy-change adjustments are not in the file and are not applied.

Reads the notes attached to each claim for descriptions of non-covered services (cosmetic, aesthetic and similar, in English and Arabic) while the claim bills a covered code. Term matching with a negation window stands in for clinical language processing.

For each provider, measures how often a refused service is followed within a short window by a different, paid code for the same patient (resubmissions and same-family recodes excluded), and compares it with other providers.
Matches every billed line against the approved disguise-risk list of code and diagnosis combinations, with the visit setting, leaving out reconstructive diagnoses and lines approved in advance.

Raises claims where the member said the billed service did not happen, or where the member's receipt names a different item from every billed service; unreliable confirmation channels lower the confidence.

num_insurers_same_event > 1 establishes that other coverage EXISTS, which is the precondition the control needs, but payer ORDER cannot be evaluated: there is no primary/secondary designation and no other-payer payment record. The signal is therefore raised as 'coordination evidence required', not as a wrong-order finding, and its confidence reflects that.
Adds the other insurers' payments, our payment and the patient share for each claim and compares the total with the allowed charge (billed less discount).
Raises claims marked as accidents, or carrying a road-traffic or work-related external-cause diagnosis, that have no liable-party record; diagnoses on the governed false-positive list are left out.
Compares what we paid on or after the date of a documented third-party settlement with what was still due once the settlement is deducted; claims already in the recovery ledger are left out.
Checks every manual override of a refusal or failed payment check for a recorded reason and an authorised role; emergency escalation and delegated authority are left out.

Compares each adjudicator's override rate on one provider's claims with colleagues' rate on the same provider and with the adjudicator's own rate elsewhere; a provider handled by one adjudicator alone is not compared.
Finds upward payment adjustments dated after a claim's first settlement and raises those with no appeal or contract true-up in the adjudication or claim-version records.

For each adjudicator and provider pair, compares the rate of full, uniform payment on claims a payment check had flagged with the rate on flagged claims elsewhere; automatically assessed claims are excluded.
Nets every payment against each cancelled or reversed claim and raises those still carrying a payment once the governed timing tolerance has passed.
Finds claim lines paid more than once beyond their payable amount (split settlements within the amount are left out) and payment references reused across providers or settlement dates.
Raises provider refunds and credits in the recovery ledger that were not applied within the governed number of days, measured to the latest date in the file.
Compares each provider's credits taken against claims they do not belong to, claims carrying negative lines, and time taken to reverse cancelled claims with other providers.

Runs as the catalogue specifies when the file carries dispensing records with the prescribed and billed product and a drug policy that lists approved equivalents; the approved product on a linked approval is also checked when approvals are present.
Runs as the catalogue specifies when the file carries dispensing records with billed and prescribed quantity, strength and form, the drug policy, and the approvals with their approved units.

Runs as the catalogue specifies when the file carries the pharmacy's own dispensing record (product and quantity handed over) and its monthly stock movements, so both can be compared with what was billed.

Runs when the file carries dispensing records and member receipts. Whether a receipt names a non-medical item is judged against a governed word list rather than a coded product catalogue; the pharmacy's stock record, when present, only raises confidence.
Runs as the catalogue specifies when the file carries each fill's date and days' supply, so the supply still in hand at the next fill of an equivalent medicine can be worked out.
Runs as the catalogue specifies when the file carries fills with days' supply and a drug policy stating the maximum treatment duration for each medicine.
Runs as the catalogue specifies when the file carries the prescriber of each fill and a clinician roster and provider register, so prescribers in one care team or provider group are counted once.
Runs as the catalogue specifies when the file carries the dispensing pharmacy and days' supply of each fill, with pharmacy stock records so stock shortages can be excluded.
Runs when the file carries daily doses, members' weights and weight-based dose limits. Only the mg-per-kg limb runs: the drug policy states no body-surface limits, so height is shown but not used.
Runs as the catalogue specifies when the file carries fills, coded diagnoses, each drug's approved indications and the step-therapy policy naming the first-line treatment that must come first.

Implemented on the pharmacy SHARE residual against diagnosis peers — the only pharmacy quantity in the source — rather than on drug volume or value. A provider whose pharmacy share sits above cfg.pharmacy_share_peer_multiple × the diagnosis-peer median is flagged. 'Without patient-mix shift' is partially controlled by the diagnosis-level peer group, not by a formal mix adjustment.

Runs as the catalogue specifies when the file carries billed wastage per line, the dose given and each drug's vial size, so billed wastage can be compared with the vial arithmetic and with other providers giving the same drug.

Runs as the catalogue specifies when the file carries prescriber and pharmacy on each fill and a roster and provider register giving each prescriber's specialty, emirate and facility for the peer comparison and the on-site exclusion.

Runs as the catalogue specifies when the file carries prescriber-to-pharmacy flows and a provider register with owners and bank, phone and address tokens; referrals are counted when a referral table is present.

Runs as the catalogue specifies when the file carries prescriber and pharmacy on each fill and a drug policy marking high-cost products; pharmacy stock records, when present, supply the product-availability exclusion.

Runs as the catalogue specifies when the file carries dated fills with prescriber and pharmacy over enough months to see a new link form; contracts, when present, supply the contract-launch exclusion.

Runs when the file carries device serials on claim lines and a device register with each serial's condition and rental or purchase status. What the line bills (new, used, rental, purchase) is read from its description; the approval and the supplier contract are not compared.

Runs when the file carries claim lines and a code reference marking implants. Any surgical procedure for the member that day counts as the qualifying procedure, operation notes are checked when documents are present, and laterality is not checked because no line records the body side.

Runs when the file carries supply lines and a device register with useful life. The usual quantity is the median billed for the same item rather than a procedure or episode norm, which the file does not state.

Runs when the file carries device serials on claim lines and a device register. The same-serial-for-several-patients limb runs in full; the limb comparing claimed stock with acquisitions is not run because the register records issued devices, not purchases.

Runs when the file carries each member's employer and sponsor and the employers' rosters: a member served while neither they nor their sponsor was on the roster is raised, as is one national-ID reference with two overlapping active covers; continuation, newborn and mandated cover are excepted.

Runs the timing limb: an add or change recorded more than the enrolment SLA after the date it takes effect, over a high-cost service already incurred, excepting approved retroactive corrections. The actor is reported but not tested, because the file holds no rule on who may make such changes.

Compares application declarations (prior cover, existing conditions) with prior cover and treatment records. Whether the law allows the comparison is approximated by a governed contestability window; privacy and non-discrimination checks remain for compliance to confirm.

days_since_policy_start supports the tenure limb exactly, and claim value supports the utilisation limb. Risk adjustment is by primary diagnosis, not by a morbidity model. previous_fraud_on_policy is used as a POLICY-HISTORY input (it is a policy attribute in the source, not the held-out outcome label) and is reported separately in the evidence so a reviewer can weigh it themselves. The catalogue's caution — 'not evidence of fraud alone' — is reproduced on the signal and the disposition is MONITOR_ONLY.

Runs when the file carries enrolment events, members' employers or brokers and providers' ownership, bank, phone and address references: a cohort of new members whose early-claim rate tops other cohorts and whose early claims go mostly to linked providers is raised, excluding enrolment campaigns and small portfolios.
